observation: agent-loop edit refactor verify rejected three correctly applied rename bundles with a rewritten-token mismatch, although every renamed token was present and exactly as the plan published it.

evidence.summary: Pre-fix: sort by startFilePos then substr at startFilePos plus a delta accumulated only from this plan own replacements.
The applier rewrites each file back-to-front against the pre-apply sha256, so it never depends on post-apply offsets.

IT-Portal reproduction: RegionConst.php expected byte 1329 but the token sat at 1221, a shift of -108 from the deleted TODO docblock; AccountingConstants.php expected 3062 and 3185 but the tokens sat at 2967 and 3090, a shift of -95. All three bundles exited 2.
OK 4 tests 21 assertions. Adds a shifted-offset case and a missing-token case; the pre-existing regression only appended text below an edit, which is why the defect went unnoticed.
End-to-end: the patched verifier re-run against the three real consumer bundles returned exit 0 each and wrote verification-result.json, unblocking the acceptance criterion the bug had blocked.
agent-loop fix commit with the two new regressions.

hypothesis: The verifier anchored each replacement at a byte position computed from the plan pre-apply offsets plus a delta built only from its own replacements, so any edit outside the plan that changed the file length above a token shifted it out from under that arithmetic.
validated_conclusion: Confirmed and fixed. Deleting resolved TODO docblocks above the renamed tokens shifted them by -108 and -95 bytes. EditMovePlanApplier never had this bug because it rewrites back-to-front and validates against the pre-apply content hash, while RefactorVerifyCommand walked forward over the current file. The verifier now searches for each replacement from a monotonic cursor and asserts the occurrence count, so a genuinely missing token still fails closed. No sibling verify command shares the arithmetic.
